assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from publisher_live at creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt. Integrity follows from the matching [5884,6024) clause digest and the full digest shared with publisher_pin. Relevance follows from section 4(a)'s express treatment of both patent and trademark rights. Interpretation follows from “held by Affirmer” and the exclusion of waiver, surrender, licensing or any other effect by the document. Applicability follows from the Statement of Purpose identifying the Affirmer who applies CC0 to the Work. Contradiction was tested against sections 1(iv), 2, 3 and 4(c) of publisher_live. The waiver and fallback each respect the exclusion, and third-party clearance is addressed separately.

challenge.method: Test section 2's broad waiver language and section 3's fallback license and nonassertion language separately against section 4(a). Compare the holder specified there with the treatment of other persons in section 4(c).
challenge.results: Section 2's breadth concerns the defined Copyright and Related Rights. Section 1(iv) even subjects unfair-competition rights to 4(a). Section 3 limits both its license and its residual nonassertion provision to the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights. Section 4(a) expressly excludes any effect on the Affirmer's patent or trademark rights. Section 4(c) separately disclaims responsibility for clearing others' rights.

limitations: The finding concerns this instrument's effect on rights held by the Affirmer. Ownership, other persons' rights, separate grants and defenses require separate evidence.
reasoning: When the Affirmer applies CC0 to a Work, section 4(a) expressly preserves patent and trademark rights held by that Affirmer. Section 2 waives the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the extent permitted by law. If that waiver is judged ineffective, section 3 licenses the exercise of those same rights to the affected extent. Section 4(a) expressly covers both surrender and licensing.
